emergence.summary: A single-gene CYP27A1 loss-of-function. CYP27A1 encodes sterol 27-hydroxylase, the mitochondrial enzyme that 27-hydroxylates sterol intermediates in the PRIMARY (classic and alternative) bile-acid synthesis pathway, a step required to make the primary bile acids chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) and cholic acid from cholesterol. CYP27A1 LOF lowers primary bile-acid synthesis THROUGHPUT, so (i) CDCA falls and (ii) -- because CDCA is the strongest feedback inhibitor of cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase (CYP7A1) -- that feedback is lost, DE-REPRESSING CYP7A1 and diverting flux down a 25-hydroxylation shunt that over-produces cholestanol and bile alcohols, which ACCUMULATE in brain, tendons (xanthomas), lens (juvenile cataracts) and arteries -> the CTX phenotype: infantile cholestasis/diarrhoea, juvenile cataracts, tendon xanthomas, and progressive adult neurodegeneration (ataxia, spasticity, cognitive decline). The emergent axis is PRIMARY BILE-ACID SYNTHESIS, driven DOWN by the deficient enzyme; the correction is to restore the missing end-product. The kit re-derives the approved replace arm: chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA; chenodiol) -- which SUPPLIES the deficient primary bile acid AND, by restoring feedback inhibition of CYP7A1, suppresses the abnormal cholestanol-producing flux (lowering plasma cholestanol and urinary bile alcohols). This is a NEW bile-acid-synthesis metabolic axis -- distinct from the kit's other lipid reads (familial hypercholesterolaemia's LDL-cholesterol LEVEL axis; sitosterolaemia's sterol-ABSORPTION axis; LAL deficiency's lysosomal neutral-lipid CATABOLISM axis) -- with an END-PRODUCT-REPLACEMENT lever (replace the missing bile acid, which also restores its own feedback). Statins / LDL apheresis lower the cholesterol substrate but do NOT restore bile-acid synthesis and are recorded as downstream-symptomatic NON-levers (the XLH/Rett downstream-agent discipline). The gamma read is of the CYP27A1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (missense/nonsense/splice across the gene), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: primary bile-acid synthesis (sterol 27-hydroxylase / CYP27A1 throughput to chenodeoxycholic acid + cholic acid; LOF -> bile-acid synthesis down, loss of CDCA feedback on CYP7A1 -> cholestanol/bile-alcohol over-production and tissue accumulation) -- a bile-acid-synthesis metabolic axis

per_gene.note: CYP27A1 encodes sterol 27-hydroxylase, the mitochondrial cytochrome-P450 that 27-hydroxylates sterol intermediates in primary bile-acid synthesis -- the step needed to form chenodeoxycholic acid and cholic acid from cholesterol. LOF lowers primary bile-acid synthesis throughput -> CDCA falls, its feedback inhibition of CYP7A1 is lost, and flux is diverted to over-produce cholestanol and bile alcohols that accumulate in tissues. As a deficient ENZYME the pathway throughput goes DOWN (with downstream accumulation of the aberrant shunt products), so the corrective lever RESTORES the end-product. Autosomal recessive, 2q35 (OMIM 606530). NCBI official symbol CYP27A1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice lesions are outside the promoter firewall.

falsifiers.claim: CYP27A1 LOF lowers primary bile-acid synthesis (CDCA down; cholestanol/bile alcohols accumulate via de-repressed CYP7A1)
falsifiers.falsifier: a CYP27A1 LOF allele that RAISED CDCA / primary bile-acid output, or that LOWERED cholestanol, would refute the throughput-down + shunt-accumulation direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: plasma CDCA and cholestanol and urinary bile-alcohol levels in CYP27A1-deficient patients vs controls

falsifiers.claim: replacing the end-product (CDCA) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if giving chenodeoxycholic acid RAISED cholestanol/bile alcohols or failed to lower them (and worsened the course), the 'replace end-product' lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: plasma cholestanol and urinary bile-alcohol response to CDCA, and the documented rebound on CDCA withdrawal (RESTORE), in CTX patients
